task.description:
WF-03 Step 2b -- hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's fix design for ISS-0106. Re-derive your verdict from lib/letflow/design/iss0106-toolchain-pin-and-format-fix.md itself and from the authoritative sources. Reading step-02-fix-design.json's result.summary and echoing it back is not validation -- it is copying a claim (core-directives.md, 'Every producing step has a validating step').

THE AUTHORITATIVE SCOPE is the section 'REVIEWER sign-off -- amendment (supersedes the version target above)' at the END of docs/migration/decisions/0005-pin-formatting-toolchain.md, dated 2026-08-21T01:25:50Z, specifically its 'Scope for the implementation (ordered; for CODE-DESIGNER)' subsection listing Parts A (7 items), B (4 files) and C (14 sites). Note that this file ALSO contains an earlier 2026-08-19 sign-off which the amendment supersedes on the version target -- a design that implements the OLD target (1.18.3/OTP 27) is wrong, and confirming which one the design targets is one of your checks.

The design's own acceptance criteria are the ten in step-02-fix-design.json's task.acceptance_criteria. Check each one against the document rather than against the producer's claim about it.

THREE THINGS DESERVE MORE THAN A CHECKLIST PASS, because each is a place where a design can look complete and still produce a task that misbehaves:

  1. **The OTP comparison rule.** `.tool-versions` pins `erlang 29.0.5`; `:erlang.system_info(:otp_release)` returns only the major release, as a charlist. A design whose rule compares those two as equal strings would report a permanent FALSE MISMATCH on a correctly-pinned host -- which destroys the warning's credibility on the one host it is supposed to reassure. Verify the design's stated rule actually produces MATCH for this host's real values. You can measure both values directly (`elixir -e` or the same mechanism the design specifies) rather than reasoning about them. Also check the design's handling of the Elixir line's `-otp-NN` suffix is CONSISTENT with its OTP rule -- if the suffix is discarded, the design must say why the `erlang` line is authoritative; if it is used, there must be a precedence rule for the two OTP verdicts disagreeing. Either is defensible; silence or contradiction is not.

  2. **Property (iii) -- the task can never alter another check's exit code.** The decision states this as a hard requirement. Check that the design makes it STRUCTURAL rather than intended. In particular verify the design's claimed mechanism (no raising call, non-raising APIs only, an outer guard) is actually sufficient, and that the specified output stream cannot interfere with a later step's result.

  3. **CODE-DESIGNER's own flagged finding, OQ1, which you must independently re-verify rather than accept or dismiss.** Because the decision mandates the new task live in `lib/mix/tasks/`, Mix must load that module to run it, which forces a project compile as the first thing `mix letflow.check` does. The hazard is that the later `compile --warnings-as-errors` step might then find nothing to recompile and pass silently -- turning a currently-failing build into an apparently-passing one, which would be the exact 'never satisfy a gate by editing what it measures' violation core-directives.md forbids. CODE-DESIGNER reports measuring this and finding the gate NOT weakened (an already-compiled project still exits 1 and re-emits all 14 warnings from the compile manifest). RE-RUN THAT MEASUREMENT YOURSELF and state the actual output -- this is the single highest-stakes claim in the design, because if it is wrong the run would ship a change that silently disarms the compile gate. Then give an explicit verdict on the residual half CODE-DESIGNER left open: if compilation fails outright, the toolchain warning may never print, partially weakening property (i). Is that material? If you judge it material, the correct outcome is NOT to design around it and NOT to FAIL the design for it -- the file path is mandated by a decision record, which binds absolutely -- but to say so plainly in result.issues and recommend ORCH route an amendment back to REVIEWER. If you judge it immaterial, say why, with reasoning about when a project that cannot compile at all would actually benefit from the warning.

VERDICT RULES: PASS only if every one of the ten acceptance criteria is genuinely met AND the three items above hold. FAIL names each unmet criterion with the specific gap and what would close it -- never a general impression. An implementation-body found in the document is an automatic FAIL on sight (the design's AC7).
acceptance_criteria: Each of the design's ten acceptance criteria (AC1..AC10 in step-02-fix-design.json) is checked against the design document itself and given an individual verdict, citing the section or line of the design that satisfies it -- or, for a failure, the specific gap

The design is confirmed to target the AMENDED pin (Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29, erlang 29.0.5) and not the superseded 2026-08-19 target, with the exact .tool-versions content it specifies quoted from the design
The OTP comparison rule is verified to produce MATCH against this host's real measured values, with the actual measured values quoted -- not reasoned about
The Elixir `-otp-NN` suffix handling is verified to be consistent with the OTP rule, and the design's stated reason (or precedence rule) is quoted
Property (iii) is assessed as structural-or-not, with the specific mechanism named and an independent judgement of whether it is sufficient

OQ1's compile-manifest measurement is RE-RUN independently and the actual command output quoted, with an explicit CONFIRMED/REFUTED verdict on CODE-DESIGNER's claim that the compile gate is not weakened
An explicit material/immaterial verdict on OQ1's residual open half (warning may not print if compilation fails outright), with reasoning, and a recommendation to ORCH if it is material
Part C's site count is independently re-derived (the design and step 01 both say 14) and either confirmed with your own measurement or reported as disagreeing, with evidence
The document is confirmed free of implementation bodies (state how you checked)
No file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step -- you validate, you do not edit the design

result.summary:
VERDICT: PASS. All ten of the design's acceptance criteria are met, and the three items singled out for more than a checklist pass hold. Verdict re-derived from lib/letflow/design/iss0106-toolchain-pin-and-format-fix.md and from the authoritative sources; step-02-fix-design.json's result.summary was NOT used as evidence for any check.

=== HIGHEST-STAKES ITEM FIRST: OQ1's compile-manifest measurement is CONFIRMED ===
Re-run independently on this host, branch feature/WF03-ISS0106-20260821, in MIX_ENV=test (matching cli/0's preferred_envs for the alias). Procedure: `MIX_ENV=test mix compile` first -> exit 0, project fully compiled, 14 warnings emitted. Then, with nothing left to recompile, `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> **EXIT 1**, `grep -c 'is expected on struct update'` -> **14**, `grep -c '^Compiling'` -> **0** (proving nothing was recompiled -- the warnings came from the compile manifest, not from a fresh compile), final line of output verbatim: `Compilation failed due to warnings while using the --warnings-as-errors option`. Repeated a second time to rule out the first run having invalidated the manifest: EXIT 1, 14 warnings, 0 Compiling lines again. CODE-DESIGNER's M5 claim is CONFIRMED exactly as stated. The task-discovery-forced compile does NOT weaken the `compile --warnings-as-errors` gate; a currently-failing build does not become an apparently-passing one. Property (iii) survives the alias-ordering side effect.

=== OQ1's RESIDUAL OPEN HALF: judged IMMATERIAL ===
Consequence (a) -- if compilation fails outright the toolchain warning may never print, partially weakening property (i). Judged IMMATERIAL, on four grounds, so NO amendment back to REVIEWER is recommended. (1) The hazard property (i) exists to prevent is named precisely in decision 0005's amendment: the warning must be on screen 'before any format diff an agent might misattribute'. When compilation fails, the `format --check-formatted` step never runs and produces no diff, so the specific misattribution (i) guards against is structurally impossible in exactly the case where the warning is lost. (2) The most likely version-caused compile failure is already self-diagnosing and strictly more informative than this warning: a host below `~> 1.18` is refused by Mix with an error that names both the required requirement and the running Elixir version, which is better information than 'expected X running Y'. (3) The only residual case -- a host within `~> 1.18` but too old for a construct in the code -- is not exercised by this tree: decision 0005's amendment measured this codebase compiling clean under 1.18.3, and Part C's idiom as version-agnostic and clean under both. So there is presently no path by which this codebase fails to compile FOR a toolchain reason inside the admitted range. (4) When it does eventually bite, the recovery cost is one command (`elixir --version`), not a debugging session. Recording it as OQ1 in the design, as CODE-DESIGNER did, is the right disposition; it should not be re-litigated as an omission.

=== PER-CRITERION VERDICTS (the design's own AC1..AC10) ===
AC1 PASS -- Parts A, B, C all covered; the amendment's seven Part-A items are addressed by number as A1..A7 (design sections 2 and 3). Item 2 is section A2, written as a verbatim instruction 'leave this line exactly as it is. Do not edit it.' with the lock-out consequence spelled out and the `~> 1.18` vs `~> 1.18.0` semantics stated. mix.exs:8 verified on disk as `elixir: "~> 1.18",`, matching the design's quotation.
AC2 PASS -- section A1 states the post-change content verbatim: `elixir 1.20.3-otp-29` / `erlang 29.0.5`, plus trailing-newline, LF, no-comment, no-blank-line constraints. Byte-identical to the amendment's block at decisions/0005 lines 180-183.
AC3 PASS -- sections A3.1-A3.7 give module `Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchain`, `use Mix.Task` with `@impl Mix.Task` on run/1, the @shortdoc text, `@spec run([String.t()]) :: :ok` always returning :ok, arguments accepted and ignored, the total parse contract (A3.3, six numbered rules), the Elixir rule (A3.4), the separate OTP rule (A3.5), and both output shapes (A3.7). The module-name -> task-name mapping is anchored to the in-repo precedent, which I verified: lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex line 1 is `defmodule Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.Test do`.
AC4 PASS -- (i)-(iv) each named with a mechanism in A3.6 rather than asserted. See the property-(iii) assessment below. One MINOR imprecision recorded in issues (A3.6(i)'s 'nothing else can print before it').
AC5 PASS -- F1..F8 in A3.7 enumerate missing / empty / no-elixir-line / no-erlang-line / malformed-recognised-line / unreadable / cwd-unavailable / unforeseen-exception, each with a message shape and each returning :ok. The AC's sixth case, 'a version string that does not parse', is resolved EXPLICITLY rather than omitted: A3.7's closing paragraph states it is not a failure mode by construction, because both comparisons are exact string equality on split strings with no numeric or Version parsing anywhere, and works two examples (`elixir abc`, `erlang -`) through to ordinary MISMATCH. That is an answer, not a silence.
AC6 PASS -- both halves re-derived by me; see the independent measurements below.
AC7 PASS -- see 'free of implementation bodies' below.
AC8 PASS -- section A4 gives the exact resulting four-element list with `letflow.check_toolchain` first. I verified the design's quotation of the CURRENT alias against mix.exs lines 56-60 on disk: it matches exactly (`format --check-formatted`, `compile --warnings-as-errors`, `letflow.check.test`).
AC9 PASS -- section 1 states B and C independent of A and of each other in any order; the single aggregate-exit-code constraint; and A3 -> A1 -> A4 landing together within Part A, with the concrete failure for each wrong order (A4 before A3 = unknown-task error; A3 before A1 = false warning, since .tool-versions on disk today does read `elixir 1.18.3-otp-27` / `erlang 27.2`, which I verified).
AC10 PASS -- `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` shows CODE-DESIGNER touched only lib/letflow/design/iss0106-toolchain-pin-and-format-fix.md plus handoffs/ and the decision record (the latter written in step 1.5 by REVIEWER, not step 2). No implementation file (.tool-versions, mix.exs, lib/mix/tasks/, or any engine file) is modified. I modified nothing outside my own handoff file.

=== AMENDED-PIN TARGETING (my AC2) CONFIRMED ===
The design targets the AMENDED 2026-08-21T01:25:50Z pin, not the superseded 2026-08-19 target. Its 'Authority' header names the amendment by date and states it supersedes the earlier sign-off on the version target. Section A1 quotes, verbatim:
    elixir 1.20.3-otp-29
    erlang 29.0.5
and names the file's current 1.18.3-otp-27 / 27.2 content as the thing being replaced -- confirmed against `cat .tool-versions` on disk. Nothing in the design implements the 1.18.3/OTP 27 target.

=== ITEM 1: THE OTP COMPARISON RULE -- VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, PRODUCES MATCH ===
Measured on this host, not reasoned about: `elixir -e 'IO.inspect(System.version()); IO.inspect(:erlang.system_info(:otp_release)); IO.inspect(List.to_string(:erlang.system_info(:otp_release)))'` ->
    "1.20.3"
    ~c"29"
    "29"
Applying the design's A3.5 rule to those real values: expected = the pinned erlang token `29.0.5` truncated at the first '.' = "29"; running = List.to_string(~c"29") = "29"; exact binary equality -> **MATCH**. Applying A3.4 to the Elixir line: `1.20.3-otp-29` split on the literal "-otp-" -> part 1 = "1.20.3"; System.version() = "1.20.3"; exact binary equality -> **MATCH**. So on a correctly-pinned host the task emits the OK line, not a mismatch block -- the permanent false-mismatch failure mode is avoided. The design's own V6 asserts this same outcome. A naive `"29.0.5" == "29"` would indeed have produced the permanent false positive; the design identifies that trap by name in A3.5 and rules against it.

=== -otp-NN SUFFIX HANDLING: CONSISTENT WITH THE OTP RULE, REASON STATED ===
The design takes the discard branch and gives the required justification rather than being silent. A3.4, quoted: 'The `-otp-NN` suffix does NOT participate in the OTP comparison, and is not compared to anything at all. It is parsed off and discarded... Reason: the suffix names the OTP major that *asdf's Elixir build* was compiled against -- a property of how the Elixir artefact was built, not a statement about the runtime. The authoritative OTP expectation is the `erlang` line. Comparing both would produce two independent OTP verdicts that can disagree, and there is no rule for which one wins.' That is exactly the 'if the suffix is discarded, the design must say why the `erlang` line is authoritative' branch, and it is consistent with A3.5, which sources the OTP expectation solely from the erlang line. No contradiction anywhere in the document. The consequence -- an internally inconsistent .tool-versions goes unflagged -- is recorded as OQ3 rather than left implicit. ACCEPTED.

=== ITEM 2: PROPERTY (iii) IS STRUCTURAL, AND THE MECHANISM IS SUFFICIENT ===
Judged STRUCTURAL, not merely intended. The design's reasoning chain is correct at its root: a Mix alias aborts only on a step that RAISES, and a step's return value is otherwise ignored -- so the task cannot touch an exit code unless it raises. Four layers then prevent that, and I assess each independently. (a) Prohibited constructs -- no Mix.raise/1, raise/1, throw/1, exit/1, System.halt/1, System.stop/1 -- a review criterion, grep-checkable, enforced as V8. Necessary but on its own only a promise about the finished file. (b) Non-raising APIs only: File.cwd/0 not File.cwd!/0, File.read/1 not File.read!/1, string splitting instead of Version.parse!/1 or String.to_integer/1. Each substitution is correct -- both bang-free forms return {:ok, _}/{:error, _} and cannot raise, and A3.2 gives the right reason for rejecting Mix.Project.project_file/0 (it raises Mix.NoProjectError). (c) THE STRUCTURAL PIECE: the entire body of run/1 is additionally guarded so any unforeseen exception becomes failure mode F8 and :ok. This is what converts (a) and (b) from 'we thought of every error' into a property that holds even if (a) or (b) were violated. The design says so in those words and I agree with the characterisation. (d) The total parse (A3.3) removes the largest class of would-be raises before the guard is ever needed -- every byte sequence maps to a {elixir_pin, erlang_pin} pair with nil for absent-or-malformed, so there is no error branch to fall off.
I also independently confirm the DANGEROUS DIRECTION of (iii) -- 'must not be capable of making a failing build look passing' -- is fully structural and does not depend on the guard at all: the task never wraps, invokes, retries or intercepts another alias step and never inspects another task's exit status, so it has no channel by which to LOWER an exit code. Its only power is to raise one (by raising), which the guard closes. The one non-obvious channel by which it could have lowered one -- the forced compile satisfying the later warnings-as-errors step -- is the M5 hazard, which I re-ran and CONFIRMED closed above.
OUTPUT STREAM CANNOT INTERFERE WITH A LATER STEP'S RESULT -- verified rather than assumed, because the alias's third step is the one string-matching gate in this repo. Warnings go to :stderr and the single OK line to :stdout via IO.puts; the later alias steps are `format --check-formatted`, `compile --warnings-as-errors` and `letflow.check.test`, none of which reads stdin or parses the parent process's accumulated output. I checked the string-matching one specifically: lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex line 63 binds `{output, exit_code} = stream_and_capture("mix", ["test"])` and lines 72/76 run String.contains?/2 against `output` -- the captured output of its OWN System.cmd subprocess (`:stderr_to_stdout`, line 103), spawned long after the toolchain task has already returned in the parent BEAM process. Nothing the toolchain task printed can enter that buffer. Additionally, every message carries the literal prefix `letflow.check_toolchain:`, which does not resemble ISS-0069's target substring. No interference by either route. SUFFICIENT.
One MINOR imprecision is recorded in issues: the design describes the outer guard as catching 'any unforeseen exception', which an implementer would naturally write as try/rescue -- and `rescue` alone catches exceptions, not throws or exits. A3.6(iii)'s prose prohibits throw/1 and exit/1, but V8's grep pattern omits `throw`. This does not change the PASS: nothing on the task's call path throws (File.read/1, File.cwd/0 and String.split/2 do not), and the residual failure direction would be a false FAILURE of the gate, never a false pass. Reported so the implementer closes it cheaply.

=== ITEM 3, second half already given above. PART C COUNT INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED: 14 CONFIRMED ===
From my own `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors` output, `grep -oE '\u2514\u2500 lib/[^:]+:[0-9]+:[0-9]+' | sort | uniq -c` yields exactly 14 distinct update sites, one occurrence each, and they match the design's C1..C14 table file:line:col for file:line:col with no discrepancy: engine.ex:1785:35; reconstruction.ex 563:24, 602:41, 619:6, 630:13, 652:28, 820:11; sub_process.ex:843:27; transition.ex 619:25, 691:10, 779:12, 845:30, 876:19, 881:31. By file: transition.ex 6, reconstruction.ex 6, sub_process.ex 1, engine.ex 1 -- matching both the design's tally and the amendment's own (decisions/0005 lines 424-426). I also confirmed there is NO OTHER WARNING CLASS: total `warning:` lines in the output = 14, all of the single class 'a struct for <S> is expected on struct update'. CONFIRMED, no disagreement to report. I additionally verified the design's cited in-repo precedent exists as described: lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:591 is `defp advance_token(%InstanceState{} = instance_state, %Token{} = token, target_node_id) do` with `%Token{token | node_id: target_node_id}` on line 592 -- exactly the shape the design tells the implementer to copy.
PART B ALSO RE-DERIVED (not required of me, but it is the other half of AC6): `mix format --check-formatted` -> exit 1, exactly four files, and the design's B1..B4 table matches the actual diff line-for-line -- variable_merge.ex 92 and 98 (the `"""` -> escaped-heredoc change), pin_resolver_test.exs 239 and 322, pin_resolver.ex 541 (the merge_effective_pins/3 head), pin_rebind_test.exs 516. No fifth file.

=== FREE OF IMPLEMENTATION BODIES (AC7) -- HOW I CHECKED ===
Three passes over the document. (1) Enumerated all 18 fence markers (9 fenced blocks) with `grep -nE '^```' `: none carries an `elixir`/`ex`/`exs` language tag, and reading each, they are -- the .tool-versions file content (A1, data, required verbatim by AC2); the quoted existing `elixir: "~> 1.18",` line; the current alias list and the target alias list (data literals, required verbatim by AC8); two message-text specifications (the OK line and the TOOLCHAIN OFF PIN block); a quoted existing markdown bullet from the developer guide; and two shell commands (`mix format --check-formatted`, `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors`). (2) Grepped for definition and body syntax: `def ` returns ONE hit, line 522, inside a Part-B table cell describing the formatting diff ('99-char `def merge_effective_pins/3` head must explode one argument per line') -- a reference to an existing head, not a definition. `defmodule`, `defp`, `case `, `cond do`, `try do`, `rescue`, `receive` -> zero hits. (3) Grepped for body markers `\bdo\b$`, `|>`, and a lone `end` line -> ZERO hits across the whole document. There is no Elixir function body anywhere in the file. The notation `%S{var | ...}` in section 3.2 is a type-shape schematic with a metasyntactic S, not code. AC7 satisfied.

=== NOTHING MODIFIED OUTSIDE handoffs/ BY THIS STEP ===
`git status --porcelain` after my work shows only: the two pre-existing ORCH files (handoffs/orchestrator.log, handoffs/registry.json) and the untracked docs/issues/ISS-0110.yaml, all left untouched per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 7, plus my own handoff file. I did not edit the design document. The only side effect of my measurements is _build/ artefacts, which is untracked. I did not run docker compose (a Postgres container is already up for this checkout).

issues.description: OQ1 residual half judged IMMATERIAL -- recorded so it is not re-litigated, NOT escalated. The design's OQ1(a) (if compilation fails outright the toolchain warning may never print) does not warrant an amendment back to REVIEWER. Reasons, in full in result.summary: the format diff that property (i) exists to protect against cannot exist when compilation fails, since the format step never runs; a host below `~> 1.18` is already refused by Mix with an error naming both the requirement and the running version, which is strictly better information than this warning; the only residual case (inside `~> 1.18` but too old for a construct in the tree) is not exercised, since decision 0005's amendment measured this codebase compiling clean under 1.18.3 and Part C's idiom as version-agnostic; and the recovery cost is one `elixir --version` invocation. ORCH does not need to route an amendment for this. CODE-DESIGNER's disposition (flag as an open question, do not design around a decision-mandated file path) was correct.

Design section A3.6, property (i), overstates its own mechanism in one sentence: 'Mix aliases execute their steps in list order, so nothing else can print before it.' That is not true on a cold build -- the task-discovery-forced compile prints before it, which the SAME document states correctly two places later (A3.6(iii)'s final bullet, and OQ1 in section 5). So this is a locally imprecise sentence corrected elsewhere in the document, not a silence or an unresolved contradiction, and it does not affect the PASS. It matters only because A3.1 requires the @moduledoc to state the mechanism for each of the four properties: the implementer must not copy this sentence into the @moduledoc verbatim, or the shipped module will carry a claim the module's own behaviour contradicts. ELIXIR-DEV should write property (i)'s @moduledoc line as 'first among the alias's own steps' rather than 'nothing can print before it'.

Property (iii)'s outer guard is specified as catching 'any unforeseen exception' (A3.6(iii), A3.7 F8), and verification V8's grep pattern is 'Mix\.raise|raise |System\.halt|System\.stop|\bexit\(' -- which omits `throw`, even though A3.6(iii)'s prose explicitly prohibits throw/1 alongside exit/1. An implementer reading 'exception' writes `try ... rescue`, and `rescue` alone does not catch a throw or an exit; those would escape the guard and abort the alias. The practical risk is nil (nothing on the call path -- File.cwd/0, File.read/1, String.split/2, List.to_string/1 -- throws or exits) and the failure direction would be a false FAILURE of the gate rather than a false pass, so this is not a PASS-blocking gap. Cheap close for ELIXIR-DEV: implement the guard as `try ... rescue ... catch ...` covering both :throw and :exit, and add `throw` to V8's grep alternation. Reported at the source so the design's next revision carries it.

result.next_action: Route to ELIXIR-DEV for implementation of the design as written -- the design is APPROVED and needs no rework; do NOT return it to CODE-DESIGNER. Pass the three MINOR issues above to ELIXIR-DEV as implementation notes, not as design defects: (1) do not copy A3.6(i)'s 'nothing else can print before it' sentence into the new task's @moduledoc, phrase it as 'first among the alias's own steps'; (2) implement property (iii)'s outer guard with `catch` as well as `rescue`, and add `throw` to V8's grep alternation when running it. Implementation order per the design's section 1: Parts B and C are independent of A and of each other and may land in any order; within Part A, item 3 (the new task) then item 1 (.tool-versions) then item 4 (the alias), those three in one commit; item 2 is a deliberate DO-NOT-EDIT of mix.exs:8; items 5, 6 are docs and order-free; item 7 is a no-op. Run the design's V1-V9 as the acceptance checks; V4 and V5 re-verify after implementation the same M5 measurement I confirmed here. No REVIEWER amendment is needed for OQ1.
